statistics.locator: Results, ANOVA for the adaptation phase (between-factor Age, within-factor Episode)
statistics.quote: We confirmed these observations by analysis of variance (ANOVA) for the adaptation phase, using the between-factor Age and the within-factor Episode: significant effects were yielded for Age (F(1,22)=7.58, P<0.05), Episode (F(14,308)=41.14, P<0.001), and their interaction (F(14,308)=3.44, P<0.001).
within_factors: Episode (15 levels; episodes 6-20 of the adaptation phase)
statistics.model_fitted_to: each subject's median initial direction error per 50-s episode during the adaptation phase
statistics.direction_quote: Most importantly, adaptive improvement was more pronounced for young than for old subjects.
statistics.admissible_reason: Main effect of Age averaged over all 15 adaptation episodes (the outcome asks about the end of adaptation only), and the p value is bounded (P<0.05) rather than exact.
statistics.notes: This is the grouping-factor effect in the paper's overall analysis of the whole adaptation phase, not a contrast at the final episode.

statistics.locator: Results, ANOVA for the adaptation phase — within-factor Episode
statistics.quote: significant effects were yielded for Age (F(1,22)=7.58, P<0.05), Episode (F(14,308)=41.14, P<0.001), and their interaction (F(14,308)=3.44, P<0.001).
within_factors: Episode (15 levels; episodes 6-20 of the adaptation phase)
statistics.model_fitted_to: each subject's median initial direction error per 50-s episode during the adaptation phase
statistics.admissible_reason: Main effect of a within-subject factor (Episode), not a between-group comparison; numerator df > 1; bounded p.

statistics.locator: Results, ANOVA for the adaptation phase — Age × Episode interaction
statistics.quote: significant effects were yielded for Age (F(1,22)=7.58, P<0.05), Episode (F(14,308)=41.14, P<0.001), and their interaction (F(14,308)=3.44, P<0.001).
within_factors: Episode (15 levels; episodes 6-20 of the adaptation phase)
statistics.model_fitted_to: each subject's median initial direction error per 50-s episode during the adaptation phase
statistics.admissible_reason: Interaction term; cannot stand in for the two groups' means.

statistics.locator: Results, ANOVA for the refresh phase
statistics.quote: Accordingly, ANOVA yielded significant effects of Age (F(1,22)=13.42, P<0.01) and Episode (F(2,44)=6.18, P<0.01), but no significant interaction.
statistics.model_fitted_to: each subject's median initial direction error per 50-s episode during the refresh phase
statistics.admissible_reason: Refers to the refresh phase after the five-minute break, not the end of the initial adaptation block; averaged over refresh episodes; bounded p.
statistics.notes: Included for completeness; measurement window differs from the outcome definition.

statistics.locator: Results, ANOVA for the refresh phase — Episode
statistics.quote: Accordingly, ANOVA yielded significant effects of Age (F(1,22)=13.42, P<0.01) and Episode (F(2,44)=6.18, P<0.01), but no significant interaction.
statistics.model_fitted_to: each subject's median initial direction error per 50-s episode during the refresh phase
statistics.admissible_reason: Within-subject main effect, numerator df > 1, wrong measurement window, bounded p.

statistics.locator: Results, additional ANOVA comparing episodes 20 and 26
statistics.quote: To determine whether the initial reduction of performance differed between age groups, we compared the pointing errors in episodes 20 and 26 by an additional ANOVA; the effects of Age (F(1,22)=13.78, P<0.01) and Episode (F(1,22)=7.79, P<0.05) were significant but not their interaction, in accordance with the view that the initial reduction was not age-dependent.
statistics.model_fitted_to: each subject's median initial direction error in episode 20 and in episode 26
statistics.admissible_reason: Main effect of Age averaged over episodes 20 and 26 (episode 26 lies after the break, outside the outcome window), and the p value is bounded (P<0.01).
statistics.notes: This is the closest test to the end of adaptation (episode 20 is the last adaptation episode), but it pools episode 20 with post-break episode 26.

statistics.locator: Results, additional ANOVA comparing episodes 20 and 26 — Episode
statistics.quote: the effects of Age (F(1,22)=13.78, P<0.01) and Episode (F(1,22)=7.79, P<0.05) were significant but not their interaction
statistics.model_fitted_to: each subject's median initial direction error in episode 20 and in episode 26
statistics.admissible_reason: Within-subject (repeated-measures) main effect, not a between-group comparison.
No standardised effect size is printed on these pages.
statistics.notes: These pages report only F values with bounded p values (and one t test for the trail-making test, a different measure), plus exponential-fit parameters (y=9.92+53.51×exp(−x/5.89) for young, y=29.51+29.91×exp(−x/5.13) for old); no Cohen's d, Hedges' g or partial eta squared is given.

parsed.notes: No test isolating the final adaptation episode (episode 20) alone is printed. The only group-factor tests on pointing error are: the mixed ANOVA over the whole adaptation phase (Age F(1,22)=7.58, P<0.05), the refresh-phase ANOVA (Age F(1,22)=13.42, P<0.01), and the episodes 20-vs-26 ANOVA (Age F(1,22)=13.78, P<0.01). All p values are bounded, so none is admissible as printed. Direction of the group difference during adaptation is stated qualitatively: 'adaptive improvement was more pronounced for young than for old subjects', i.e. older subjects had larger errors. The t test on page 3 (t(22)=5.25; P<0.001) belongs to the trail-making test, a different measure, and is not reported here.
